calibration_packet.description: Structured calibration packet for evaluating candidate solutions to the mislabeled-envelope puzzle using audit criteria C1-C8

strategy_structure.step_1: Inspect 1 item from the Mixed-labeled envelope (known pure since all labels wrong). Record the identified pure type.
strategy_structure.step_2: Inspect 14 items from a second envelope. If all 14 match the identified pure type, the envelope is pure. If any differ, it's the 7/13 mixed envelope.
strategy_structure.step_3: The remaining two envelopes are fixed by elimination using the all-labels-wrong constraint.

canonical_answer.rationale: The mixed envelope has a 7/13 split, so it cannot produce more than 13 consecutive items of the same type. 14 draws guarantees distinguishing pure from mixed.

C1_correct_final_answer.true_when: Solution states the actual minimum guaranteed number of inspections (15) as a single committed final value
false_when: Gives a different number
Gives multiple conflicting final answers
Never states a final minimum
Gives a range ('15 or more')
Lists alternatives ('either 15 or 16')

C2_concrete_strategy.true_when: Solution specifies an explicit multi-branch inspection strategy with: (a) which envelopes are inspected, (b) how many items are drawn from each, (c) how the strategy adapts to observations, (d) how labels are fixed after observations
false_when: Only gives a number without strategy
Gives vague ideas without concrete rules
Does not connect proposed number to concrete strategy
Oscillates among incompatible inspection counts without committing
Closing synthesis is hand-wavy ('forced by contradiction', 'remaining are determined') without showing per-branch label-fixing
Acknowledges single-draw ambiguity then concludes 'enough information has been gathered' without specifying branch-by-branch rules

C3_valid_upper_bound.true_when: Solution correctly proves proposed number is sufficient to guarantee correct relabeling in every possible legal arrangement and every observation sequence
false_when: Proof only works in favorable branches
Proof depends on luck
Leaves multiple labelings possible in some branch
Does not show how all four labels are fixed
Works only when second inspection returns identified pure type
Fails on 7/13 mixed-envelope worst-case branch

C4_valid_lower_bound.true_when: Solution correctly proves fewer inspections cannot guarantee success by ruling out ALL strategies using fewer inspections (not just the proposed one)
acceptable_methods: Indistinguishable-case reasoning: construct two legal envelope arrangements producing identical observations under smaller budget but requiring different final labels
false_when: No lower-bound argument given
Only asserts minimality
Argues only that its own strategy would need more draws
Arithmetic derivation from response's own strategy without impossibility proof
No construction of adversarial cases

C5_worst_case_guarantee.true_when: Solution treats problem as worst-case guarantee, explicitly addressing unlucky-draw branches and showing strategy still succeeds
false_when: Relies on probability
Uses expected outcomes
Assumes 'likely' outcomes
Depends on lucky draws
Only considers favorable cases
Stops at one particular observation sequence
Treats favorable single-draw observations as resolving worst-case ambiguity

remains_true_when: Single-draw observation is from Mixed-labeled envelope (label known wrong, inference valid)
Response acknowledges single-draw ambiguity ('this envelope is either mixed or purely X') without collapsing to purity claim
Response's strategy is merely insufficient without explicit single-draw purity claim
false_when: Claims one observed sequence from envelope that could still be mixed proves the envelope is pure
Infers envelope is pure T from one type-T draw without 14-draw verification
Load-bearing two-draw purity inference (against 7/13 mixed envelope returning 13 of one type)
C6_no_invalid_one_draw_inference.key_boundary: False only when explicit single-draw purity claim is the load-bearing inference

C7_no_exact_mixed_pair_requirement.true_when: Strategy works without requiring identification of which two pure types compose the mixed envelope
false_when: Solution adds extra inspections solely because it thinks exact two-type composition of mixed envelope must be identified
Says 'we then take a second sequence to identify which two types are combined'
C7_no_exact_mixed_pair_requirement.acceptable: If strategy incidentally discovers exact mixed pair without requiring it for labeling

false_when: Says envelope known mislabeled with 'Mixed' might actually be the mixed envelope
Treats pure-labeled envelopes as if their labels were correct
Says remaining labels are forced when multiple legal assignments remain possible
Confuses possible success path with guaranteed strategy
Treats probability argument as guarantee
'Determined automatically by elimination' after too-few observations
'The remaining are forced by contradiction' when not actually forced
'The remaining labels cycle uniquely'
'Enough information has been gathered to deduce final arrangement uniquely' after acknowledged ambiguity
'Must be' claims where only 'could be' is justified
'Assignment follows directly' from single observations when it doesn't
C8_no_fatal_wrong_claim.note: C8 FALSE is INDEPENDENT of C3 and of the primary_failure_code

verdict_rule.ACCEPT: if and only if all criteria C1 through C8 are true
verdict_rule.note: Correct final answer with invalid reasoning must be rejected

disambiguation_order.condition: Response oscillates among incompatible inspection counts and never settles
Final stated number does not equal canonical minimum (15) and strategy is otherwise structurally complete
Strategy missing concrete branch-by-branch label-fixing rules (e.g., hand-wavy 'forced by contradiction')
disambiguation_order.overrides: Downstream defects that follow from missing strategy

disambiguation_order.condition: Load-bearing one-draw purity inference from possibly-mixed envelope drives proposed minimum
Response acknowledges worst-case framing for one envelope but abandons it for others, or treats favorable observations as resolving ambiguity
Adds extra inspections solely to determine exact two-type composition of mixed envelope
Strategy structurally complete with correct number, valid upper bound, worst-case framing, but no impossibility argument given
Upper-bound argument leaves multiple legal labelings open in some worst-case branch
Load-bearing defect is proof-invalidating 'forced' or 'cycle uniquely' assertion when multiple legal labelings remain open

C2_concrete_strategy.TRUE_only_when: Response specifies multi-branch plan: which envelopes inspected, how many items drawn, what each observation implies, how each branch fixes all four labels
FALSE_when: Single-inspection plan followed by 'forced by contradiction' or 'remaining are determined'
Oscillates among multiple incompatible inspection counts without committing
Acknowledges single-draw ambiguity and concludes 'enough information has been gathered' without branch-by-branch rules

C4_valid_lower_bound.TRUE_only_when: Response constructs indistinguishable-case argument exhibiting two legal envelope arrangements producing identical observations under strictly smaller budget
C4_valid_lower_bound.FALSE_when: Arithmetic derivation from response's own strategy without exhibiting adversarial cases

C6_no_invalid_one_draw_inference.FALSE_only_when: Response explicitly treats one observed sequence from envelope that could still be mixed as proving envelope is pure (without 14-draw verification)
NOT_FALSE_when: Acknowledges ambiguity without collapsing to purity claim
Strategy merely insufficient without explicit single-draw claim

FALSE_when_triggering_phrases: 'determined automatically by elimination' after too-few observations
'enough information has been gathered to deduce the final arrangement uniquely' after acknowledged ambiguity
'the assignment follows directly' from single observations

walked_scoring_example.scenario: Inspect two items from each of three envelopes (6 inspections total), label by majority type; if all three show distinct types, fourth is mixed; concludes 'minimum is 6'

evaluation.C2_reason: Strategy explicit: which envelopes, how many items, how labels assigned
evaluation.C3_reason: In branch where mixed envelope's two drawn items match pure envelope's type, assignment is ambiguous
evaluation.C4_reason: No impossibility proof for fewer than 6 inspections
evaluation.C5_reason: Strategy depends on favorable observation pattern
evaluation.C6_reason: Infers envelope's pure type from two same-type draws, insufficient against 7/13 mixed envelope
evaluation.C7_reason: Strategy does not require identifying exact mixed pair
evaluation.C8_reason: 'If all three show distinct types, fourth is mixed' is load-bearing claim failing on adversarial draws

walked_scoring_example.primary_code_reason: Load-bearing defect is two-draw purity inference, not arithmetic of final count

common_anti_patterns.fatal_elimination_claim: Asserting 'all labels are wrong' forces specific assignment after single observation (derangement still leaves multiple legal assignments)
common_anti_patterns.invalid_purity_inference: Treating one observation per envelope as identifying that envelope's pure type (violates C6 when envelope could still be mixed)
common_anti_patterns.unnecessary_mixed_pair_id: Inflating count by adding draws 'to determine exact mixed pair' (task only requires labeling mixed envelope correctly)
common_anti_patterns.invalid_minimality_claim: Claiming minimality because response's own strategy could not be reduced (must rule out ALL strategies)
common_anti_patterns.probability_as_guarantee: Treating probability-of-success argument as worst-case guarantee
common_anti_patterns.possible_vs_guaranteed: Confusing possible success path with guaranteed strategy (guarantee must succeed on every legal branch)

key_glossary.envelope: One of four physical containers, each labeled with sequence type that is necessarily wrong
key_glossary.pure_envelope: Envelope whose 20 sequences are all one type (Strictly Increasing, Strictly Decreasing, or Constant)
key_glossary.mixed_envelope: Envelope whose 20 sequences split 7/13 between two of three sequence types
key_glossary.pure_labeled_envelope: Envelope labeled with pure-type string ('Strictly Increasing', 'Strictly Decreasing', 'Constant') - either pure envelope of different type or mixed envelope
key_glossary.mixed_labeled_envelope: Envelope labeled 'Mixed' - necessarily pure since all labels wrong
key_glossary.worst_case_guarantee: Strategy correct for every legal envelope arrangement and every adversarial draw sequence
key_glossary.indistinguishable_case_argument: Lower-bound technique constructing two legal arrangements producing identical observations under smaller budget
key_glossary.identified_pure_type: Sequence type observed in first draw from Mixed-labeled envelope (single observation suffices since envelope known pure)
